title: John R. Bassler, DrPH, MS
text:
About
As an experienced statistician, I’ve honed my skills in higher education, contributing to research and analytical initiatives. I apply advanced spatial and survival statistical methods to public health challenges, with a focus on HIV care outcomes across Alabama and the Deep South.
I currently serve as Clinical Database Manager II with the UAB Center for AIDS Research (CFAR), and I am completing my Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) in Biostatistics at UAB, with a dissertation on shared frailty models for spatial data applied to time to HIV viral suppression. My work sits at the intersection of survival analysis, spatial and Bayesian statistical methods, and structural determinants of HIV care outcomes — including a study on historical redlining and delays in HIV treatment that has been covered in the national press.

title: John R. Bassler
text: It has been a privilege to be a member of the Council for Emerging and New Statisticians (CENS) since 2024. CENS operates under the Eastern North American Region (ENAR) of the International Biometric Society (IBS), and supports students and early-career statisticians through mentorship, networking, and professional development. I served on the Steering Committee in 2025, and I’m now serving as Co-Chair, a role I began in 2026.

title: Teaching
text: Teaching statistics is an exercise in translation — finding creative ways to make rigorous methods accessible to students who arrive with very different quantitative backgrounds, from undergraduate honors students to graduate students in biostatistics, epidemiology, and nursing. Whether leading a course, guest lecturing, working one-on-one as a TA, or explaining a concept to a collaborator, I try to keep the material grounded in the applied public health problems that drew me to it in the first place.
